decisions.reason: The water phantom is adjacent to the firm's core dosimetry knowledge and research-facing customer base, but its niche particle-therapy market and slower commercialization signals make it somewhat riskier than the chamber products.
A small volume ionization chamber fits the firm's existing measurement and detector capabilities closely, so management is likely to keep it and refine it using accumulated application knowledge.
This product also builds directly on the firm's established ionization-chamber expertise, though overlap with other chamber variants raises some portfolio-rationalization risk.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is highly aligned with the firm's core technological base and customer needs, making continued commercialization the most likely choice.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry is a natural extension of the firm's absorbed know-how in radiotherapy measurement and should be improvable through routine R&D and user feedback.

A thimble ionization chamber is a classic, closely related product for this type of specialist German instrument maker, so the firm would usually retain it unless evidence of failure were much stronger.
